title: Evidence of the Cooper-Pair Field with Gaussian Memory Kernel in Unconventional Superconductors
abstract: We develop a dynamical description of the superconducting pair field in which the Cooper-channel Hubbard--Stratonovich field $Δ$ is treated as a memory-dressed Bogoliubov pair field rather than as a purely static order parameter. Starting from the standard pair-field effective action, we couple $Δ$ to antinode-selected collective or self-generated fields. An ensemble of such modes produces a distribution of local Bogoliubov frequencies; when this distribution is approximately Gaussian, ensemble averaging gives the memory factor $\exp[-t^2/(2τ_g^2)]$. In cuprate superconductors, the antinodal gap or pseudogap restricts the active electronic phase space and acts as a momentum-space spectral cavity. It selects fluctuation wavevectors $\mathbf Q_a$ that may become charge-density-wave-like instabilities in an ordered limit, but behave as a reservoir of local collective fields in the fluctuating regime. The same framework admits resonant algebraic prefactors, so that threshold and forced-oscillator responses generate the hierarchy $p=-1/2,1/2,1,3/2,\ldots$, while the Gaussian envelope cuts off secular growth and converts these branches into finite spectral components. The resulting picture contains a robust pseudogap memory channel and, below $T_c$, an additional condensate-assisted coherent channel proportional to $|Δ_0(T)|^2$. Thus the superconducting transition primarily reorganizes pair-field spectral weight between incoherent pseudogap memory and coherent Bogoliubov memory. The frequency-domain response is expressed in terms of parabolic-cylinder functions, and comparisons with Raman, ARPES, tunneling, and doping-dependent ARPES scaling suggest that these probes are complementary projections of the same Gaussian-memory pair continuum. We compare our numerical results with the recent experimental data on Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$.
summary: This work develops a dynamic theory for superconductivity in unconventional materials by treating the superconducting pair field as having memory effects due to local electronic fluctuations. It unifies spectroscopic measurements like ARPES and Raman scattering into a single framework governed by Gaussian-memory parabolic-cylinder functions, providing a detailed picture of how spectral weight shifts across different energy scales during the superconducting transition.
main_problem: To develop a dynamical description of the superconducting pair field that treats it as a memory-dressed Bogoliubov pair field, moving beyond static order parameter approximations.
main_result: The superconducting transition reorganizes spectral weight between an incoherent pseudogap memory channel and a coherent condensate-assisted Bogoliubov memory channel. The response is unified by a Gaussian-memory Parabolic-Cylinder Function (PCF) framework.
method: The authors derive the dynamics by coupling the pair field to fluctuating local modes, leading to an ensemble average that introduces a characteristic Gaussian memory factor into the effective action.
model_or_system: The model focuses on unconventional superconductors, specifically cuprates like Bi2Sr2CaCu2O(8+d). The theory uses the Cooper-channel Hubbard-Stratonovich field ($\Delta$) and incorporates fluctuations arising from momentum-space spectral cavities (the pseudogap).
key_observables: Frequency-domain response expressed via parabolic-cylinder functions; measurable quantities include Raman spectra, ARPES background signatures, and superconducting gap features.
important_parameters: Critical temperatures ($T^*$, $T_{	ext{pair}}$, $T_c$); characteristic dephasing times ($	au_{	ext{pg}}, 	au_{	ext{sc}}$); algebraic power laws ($p=-1/2, 1/2, 1, \dots$).
main_assumptions: The ensemble averaging of local frequency shifts is approximated as Gaussian to yield the exponential memory factor. The framework assumes that different spectroscopic probes are projections of a single underlying PCF continuum.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the need for dynamic pair-field treatment, deriving the memory kernel via ensemble averaging over local fluctuations, and finally unifying the resulting spectral features (pseudogap, superconducting) within a single PCF mathematical structure.
why_interesting: The use of memory effects derived from statistical ensembles to describe phase transitions is highly relevant to open quantum systems dynamics. The connection between spectral weight redistribution and structured decay envelopes provides a powerful tool for analyzing complex many-body relaxation processes.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Raman electronic susceptibility in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ compared with the memory- dressed response. Blue points denote the extracted experimental spectrum at 15 K [12], the red dashed line is the fitted total response Eq. (55), which is composed of Cr = 0.11, the gray line is from the PCF term with Ar = 2.24, the green line is from the Gaussian Gr(E) term, and the black trace shows the residual. The narrower Gr(E) contribution is tentatively associated with the B1g phonon mode centered near 34 meV.

Figure 2: Temperature-dependent antinodal ARPES spectra compared with memory-dressed fits: 6 K (upper left), 60 K (upper right), 70 K (lower left), and 80 K (lower right). Blue points show the extracted intensity from Chen et al. [13] and red curves show the results of Eq. (66) with Apg = 1.27 and Asc(0) = 1.93 in arb units. The sequence illustrates a robust pseudogap memory background together with a resonant Bogoliubov component that weakens on approaching the reported Tc = 77 K and may retain incoherent spectral weight slightly above Tc up to the fitted crossover scale Tpair.

Figure 3: Tunneling differential conductance at low temperature compared with the memory- dressed density-of-states model. Blue points denote the background-removed dI/dV data, derived from the experimental data [14] and the red curve denotes the fitted response, Eqs. (61) and (67). The agreement of the coherence features and the broader background provides a cross-probe consistency check between ARPES and tunneling.
